study_identification.title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

study_characteristics.study_objective: The study aimed to map deviations from normative ranges of brain structure for individual patients with schizophrenia and evaluate whether the loci of individual deviations recapitulated group-average brain maps of schizophrenia pathology.

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants showing gross artifacts, cerebellar cropping and/or significant head motion were excluded. Six individuals with schizophrenia were excluded due to artifacts (movement, ghosting and/or signal dropout).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Retrospective harmonization of diffusion-weighted images using a nonlinear mapping of rotation invariant spherical harmonics features. A reference site was selected (Brisbane), and age and sex-matched healthy controls from other sites were used to compute the mapping.

predictor_effects.answer: The model included sex, age, age-squared (if justified), and acquisition site as nuisance confounds, treated as fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model explicitly includes acquisition site as a nuisance confound. The paper also mentions that inter-site differences were minimized through calibration and harmonization.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Ci encapsulates nuisance confounds, including acquisition site. ... An individual traveled to all five sites and was scanned at each site to quantify gross inter-site differences. A Siemens MRI phantom was also scanned at each site to enable inter-site calibration. This calibration was done prior the data collection to help minimize the inter-site variability caused by the scanner. In addition, in this study, the diffusion-weighted images were retrospectively harmonized to alleviate possible nonlinear site-related differences.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Not available in the provided text.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation on the training set itself (e.g., by examining residuals).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study used a tenfold cross-validation framework to validate the normative model on held-out healthy individuals.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: To this end, percentile curves were fitted using a randomly selected subset of healthy individuals (n = 175, training set) and the proportion of remaining healthy individuals residing within the 5–95% percentiles (normative range) was enumerated (n = 20, test set). This was repeated for 20 randomly selected test-training subsets, using a tenfold cross-validation framework. For all cortical regions and white matter tracts, more than 90% of the healthy individuals in each test set resided within the normative range (Supplementary Fig. 3), confirming that the normative models were not predicting an excessive number of deviations

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not validate the model on an external dataset from a different domain.

deviation_metric.answer: z-scores from the 5th and 95th percentiles. Individuals were classified as infra-normal (z5 < -1.96) or supra-normal (z95 > 1.96).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Correlation between polygenic risk score (PRS) and the average abnormality index (AAI). Canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to find associations between deviation scores and PRS, and between deviation scores and symptom dimensions. Also, correlations between AAI and IQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Anatomical loci of schizophrenia-related changes are highly heterogeneous across individuals, and group-consensus pathological maps are not representative of most individual patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: While group-level analyses showed widespread reductions in FA and CT in schizophrenia, normative modeling revealed that no more than 15-20% of patients deviated from the normal range for any single brain region. However, 79% of patients showed at least one infra-normal deviation. Higher polygenic risk for schizophrenia was associated with a greater number of infra-normal CT deviations (r = -0.17), particularly in temporal regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Limitations include the potential for noise in MRI data, incomplete reproducibility of deviation maps for smaller acquisition sites, the subjective definition of the normative range (5-95th percentiles), and the need for larger normative samples. Other limitations are the potential influence of medication, illness duration, and the use of quantile regression instead of other methods.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling can help parse schizophrenia heterogeneity and guide personalized medicine, such as identifying targets for neural stimulation or selecting antipsychotic drugs.

general_notes.general_notes: The study highlights the discrepancy between group-level findings and individual patient profiles in schizophrenia research, emphasizing the importance of personalized approaches.
